# Every line is a verdict and the command it is the verdict for, read
# against testdata/policy.yaml. One command per kind of question, and a
# pair only where the pair is the question. Changing how anything is
# matched means writing down here which answers changed.

# A denied command
deny    dd if=/dev/zero of=/dev/sda

# A denied pattern
deny    rm -rf /

# A denied git subcommand, however the command is spelled
deny    git push origin main

# An allowed command
allow   ls -la

# Assignments in front of a command are passed over to reach it, hide
# nothing from a denial, and count only where they really are
# assignments: `a-b` is no name a shell would take, so that command is
# `a-b=1` and not `ls`.
allow   A=1 B=2 ls -la
deny    ENV=1 dd if=/dev/zero of=/dev/sda
ask     a-b=1 ls -la

# A program whose name merely opens with one the policy names
ask     lsblk

# A command the policy says nothing about
ask     nmap localhost

# A dangerous command behind a program that runs it
deny    bash bin/publish

# A safe command reading a file named after a dangerous one. `cat`
# accounts for the program and not the file, so it answers for neither
# of these commands whole and takes neither denial off the table.
deny    cat bin/publish
deny    cat dd

# A denied command named inside code handed to an interpreter the
# policy allows
deny    python3 -c "__import__('os').system('dd if=/dev/zero of=/dev/sda')"

# A line is denied for any one command, allowed only for every one of
# them, and asked about for anything in between
deny    ls && dd if=/dev/zero of=/dev/sda
allow   ls && cat notes.txt
ask     nmap localhost && ls -la

# A repository reached into has to be one the policy trusts
allow   git -C /work status
ask     git -C /elsewhere status

# A repository is one the policy trusts only when it is written out.
# One the shell has yet to work out could be anywhere.
allow   git -C "/work" status
ask     git -C "$REPO" status
ask     git -C ~nobody/work status

# A path rule never judges a command, even one that is only the path
ask     ~/.ssh/id_rsa

# An assignment in front of a command can point it at another
# repository. Git reads GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE and GIT_NAMESPACE as the
# options they stand for, and so are they judged. Any other assignment
# points it nowhere.
#
# Denied, as they would be without the assignment:
deny    GIT_DIR=/work/.git git push origin main
deny    GIT_TRACE=1 git -C /work/app push origin main
#
# Allowed, pointed into a trusted repository or pointed nowhere:
allow   GIT_DIR=/work/.git git status
allow   GIT_TRACE=1 git -C /work status
allow   GIT_TRACE=1 git -C /work/app push origin topic
#
# Contested, where the assignment is what takes a command out of the
# repository a rule vouches for. A push is refused wherever git's
# repository is named, since the config it names can send the commits
# anywhere.
ask     GIT_DIR=/elsewhere/.git git status
ask     GIT_WORK_TREE=/elsewhere git -C /work status
allow   git -C /work/app push origin topic
deny    GIT_DIR=/elsewhere/.git git -C /work/app push origin topic
deny    GIT_DIR=/work/app/.git git -C /work/app push origin topic
